# Installable Book

This site is an installable book powered by Spw. It starts as plain HTML with
progressive enhancement and a CSS cascade architecture built on substrate tokens.
The book concept is the default frame — accessible to writers, ebook authors, and
anyone building a deep media presence. Production seasons, studio binding, and
broadcast-style cycles are available as vocabulary when you need them.

## Architecture

The `.spw/` directory declares what the show is:
- `.spw/index.spw` — routing table and surface registry
- `.spw/mount.spw` — studio binding, deployment targets, writers room permissions
- `.spw/origin.spw` — the generative seed (concept, painting, NFT) and chromatic palette
- `.spw/containers.spw` — chunking scheme, narrative containers, CSS container mapping
- `.spw/anchors.spw` — cultural precipitation tracking and merchandise readiness
- `.spw/workspace.spw` — workspace roots and LSP configuration

## CSS Cascade Layers (in order)

1. `reset` — browser normalization
2. `substrate` — semantic token vocabulary (--spw-ground, --spw-accent, --spw-beat, etc.)
3. `structure` — page grid, shell, type baseline
4. `region` — named zones (nav, hero, main, footer)
5. `component` — panels, buttons, badges, callouts
6. `season` — swappable per production cycle, overrides substrate tokens
7. `override` — ephemeral one-offs

All CSS values trace to substrate tokens. No magic numbers.
Swap `/assets/season.css` to change the show's visual identity without touching structure.

## Editing Model

- Edit public HTML pages directly.
- Keep pages legible without JavaScript.
- Use `public/fragments/` for shared navigation and footer.
- Use `public/http/get/*.json` for route and show metadata.
- Use `data-spw-region` attributes to identify named layout zones.
- Use `data-spw-container` attributes for narrative chunking boundaries.
- Use `data-spw-affect` for valence pentad branding (boon/bane/bone/bonk/honk).

## High-Value Editable Surfaces

- `/index.html` — landing page, install prompt, show positioning
- `/chapters/index.html` — table of contents / episode listing
- `/chapters/01-opening/index.html` — first live episode
- `/places/index.html`, `/items/index.html`, `/artifacts/index.html` — route family indexes
- `/fragments/site-nav.html`, `/fragments/site-footer.html` — shared shell
- `/assets/substrate.css` — token vocabulary (showrunner-controlled)
- `/assets/season.css` — season aesthetic (swappable)
- `/http/get/show.json` — show metadata, studio, season, origin
- `/http/get/site.json` — site contract, CSS architecture, editing model
- `/http/get/chapters.json` — episode manifest

## Route Families and Lifecycle

- `/chapters/:slug/` — permanent (persists across seasons)
- `/places/:slug/` — permanent
- `/items/:slug/` — seasonal (archives when production cycle ends)
- `/artifacts/:slug.html` — ephemeral (dissolves, content may re-precipitate)
- `/seasons/:number/` — archivable (moves from live to collected)

## PWA Surfaces

- `/manifest.webmanifest`
- `/sw.js`
- `/offline.html`

## Conventions

- Prefer `chapters/01-slug/` over `chapter/01`.
- Treat `enhancements.js` as progressive enhancement only.
- If adding a framework or backend, preserve the route contract first.
- Season swap = drop a new season.css. Structure and components stay.
